key_insight: A differentiable Schwarz-coupled solver combines near-wall and bulk transport models with agentic AI optimization for inverse modeling of thin boundary layers.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets high-Péclet-number transport, where resolving steep near-wall gradients can make simulation and parameter estimation computationally expensive.
method: Split near-wall and bulk dynamics into overlapping finite-element subdomains coupled by Schwarz iteration.
Use adjoint sensitivities for inverse optimization with governing equations and boundary conditions enforced as hard constraints.
Compare LLM-proposed parameter updates with an AI agent that manages multistage optimization and expands a functional basis under a prescribed admission policy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower computational cost than a single-domain formulation and greater agentic AI benefit for functional-basis unknowns than nodal fields, without quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the chosen functional basis and admission policy; the abstract does not establish robustness across transport regimes.
paper_title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
